Good morning, Mr. Sharma. Please, have a seat. What brings you in today? Good morning, doctor. Thank you. For the past three or four days, I've been having some trouble with my right eye. It feels quite dry, it gets red by the end of the day, and my vision gets a bit blurry when I'm working on my laptop. I see. Are you experiencing any pain, discharge, or sensitivity to light?
No severe pain, just a mild gritty sensation, like there's a grain of sand stuck in it. No discharge, but my eye waters occasionally when I strain. Doctor. All right. How many hours a day do you typically spend looking at screens? Patient. Quite a bit, actually. Around eight to ten hours a day for work, plus using my phone in the evening. Doctor. That's very common. Let's do a quick physical examination first.
We'll check your vision using the eye chart and take a look at the front of your eye using the slit lamp microscope. The doctor conducts the visual acuity test and examines the patient's eyes with the slit lamp. Doctor. Everything structurally looks healthy. Your retina and intraocular pressure are normal, and there's no sign of infection. What you're experiencing is classic digital eye strain combined with dry eye syndrome.
If you've been on screens for long periods, our blink rate drops by about 50%, which causes the tear film on the eye surface to dry out quickly. Patient. Ah, that makes sense. I definitely forget to take breaks. Is it reversible, doctor? Doctor. Absolutely. Here is what we'll do. Lubricating eye drops. I'm prescribing preservative-free artificial tears.
Keep them hydrated. The 20-20-20 rule. Every 20 minutes of screen time, look at something at least 20 feet away for 20 seconds. This relaxes your eyes-focusing muscles. Screen ergonomics. Keep your screen about an arm's length away, positioned slightly below eye level, and adjust the brightness so it matches your room lighting. Patient. That sounds very manageable.
Doctor. Try this routine for two weeks. If the dryness or blurriness doesn't improve, or if you develop severe pain or sudden vision changes, come back sooner. Otherwise, you should start feeling relief within a few days. Patient. Thank you so much, doctor. I'll start using the drops today and stick to the 20-20-20 rule. Doctor. You're very welcome. Take care.
